direct_answer: Steroids for polymyalgia rheumatica are reduced slowly over many months. Steroids can contribute to muscle weakness, bone thinning and other side effects, especially in older people. Never stop suddenly. Strength exercise and bone protection, if advised, can help.
author: Louis Maxwell

content:
Steroids work well for PMR, but long courses can affect muscles and bones.

This guide explains tapering and staying strong. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

How tapering works

Your doctor reduces the dose gradually. Symptoms can return as the dose falls; tell your GP if they do.

Side effects to know about

  • Muscle weakness, especially in thighs.
  • Bone thinning.
  • Raised blood sugar.
  • Mood or sleep changes.

Staying strong

  • Sit-to-stand practice.
  • Gentle leg strength work.
  • Walking as able.
  • Ask a physiotherapist.

Bone protection

Ask whether you need bone protection or a bone density check.

Steroid safety

Carry a steroid card if given one, and do not stop steroids suddenly.

When to get help

  • Get urgent same-day help for new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing or vision changes.
  • Get urgent help if you are unwell, vomiting and unable to take your steroids.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I stop if I feel better?

No; follow your plan.

Is weakness permanent?

It may improve with exercise and lower doses.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Polymyalgia rheumatica
  • NHS: Prednisolone
  • NHS: Steroids
